<issue>
A re-fetch that never gets a response truncates the mirrored file to zero on macOS
On the macOS CI runner, a re-fetch whose connection dies before the status line arrives overwrites the mirrored file with zero bytes. The same crawl on Linux leaves the previous copy alone.

Seen in run 30220185765 (job "build (macOS arm64, clang)"), on a fixture that serves `/changes/reset.bin` in full on the first fetch and, on every fetch after that, closes the connection without answering. The change report for pass 2 puts the file under `changed` with:

```
{ "url": ".../changes/reset.bin", "file": "127.0.0.1_50718/changes/reset.bin", "size": 0, "previous_size": 2062 }
```

`size` is a plain `fsize_utf8()` of the path after the crawl, so the 2062 bytes pass 1 mirrored are gone and a zero-length file is in their place. Three attempts (`--retries=2`) all failed, so nothing was ever received to write.

The suspect is the save gate in `htscore.c` (around the "An empty body must not overwrite the file when the transfer failed" comment): it lets a zero-length body through on `r.size == 0 && r.statuscode > 0`. If the Darwin socket path leaves a positive status code behind on a connection that produced no response, `filesave()` runs and truncates. I have not reproduced it locally, so which of the two differs, the status code or the body pointer, is still open.

Related to #746 and to the #562 family: a failed re-fetch must not damage the copy it failed to refresh. This one destroys the bytes directly rather than through the purge.


</issue>

The repository is at /testbed.

input.instruction: In /testbed, open src/htscore.c and find the comment "An empty body must not overwrite the file when the transfer failed". Print ~60 lines of context around it with line numbers.

content.content: {"summary":"The comment is at src/htscore.c:1983, in httpmirror's non-HTML save path. It sits just before the filesave call. The guard `if (r.adr != NULL || (r.size == 0 && r.statuscode > 0))` stops a failed transfer (statuscode <= 0, e.g. an -M hard-stop) from truncating a good copy to 0 bytes.","findings":["src/htscore.c:1982-1985: comment block 'ATTENTION C'EST ICI QU'ON SAUVE LE FICHIER!!' followed by the 'An empty body must not overwrite...' comment (#77 follow-up).","src/htscore.c:1986: guard `if (r.adr != NULL || (r.size == 0 && r.statuscode > 0))`.","src/htscore.c:1987-1988: inside the guard, file_notify() and then filesave(opt, r.adr, r.size, savename(), urladr(), urlfil()).","src/htscore.c:1990-1998: on filesave failure, check_fatal_io_errno() sets exit_xh=-1 and logs 'Unable to save file'.","src/htscore.c:1968-1980: just before it, the non-html branch logs 'Store ...' or 'non-html file ignored after upload', and in the ignored case frees r.adr."],"confidence":0.97}

input.instruction: In /testbed/src, look at htslib.c (htsrequest / hts_request / http_xfread1 / back_* in htsback.c) for how r.statuscode, r.msg, r.adr are set when a connection closes before any status line is received (retries). Report where statuscode could stay positive (e.g. initialised to nonzero, or set to a value like HTTP_OK before headers). Also report what statuscode values mean failure (STATUSCODE_* constants) and whether 'r.adr == NULL' for a successful empty 200 body.

content.content: {"summary":"A connection that closes before any status line is received ends up with statuscode HTTP_OK (200) and msg 'Unknown, assuming junky server' on the synchronous paths. The code initialises statuscode to a failure value, but treatfirstline() overwrites it with 200 when the status line is empty. I did not read the back_wait path at htsback.c:3599 and :3651 in detail. I did not find where a successful empty 200 body sets r.adr, so I could not answer that part.","findings":["Failure constants are in htsbasenet.h:142-150: INVALID=-1, TIMEOUT=-2, SLOW=-3, CONNERROR=-4, NON_FATAL=-5, SSL_HANDSHAKE=-6, TOO_BIG=-7, TEST_OK=-10 (a test result, not a real failure), EXCLUDED=-11. Every failure is negative; real HTTP codes are positive.","hts_init_htsblk (htslib.c:646) sets statuscode = STATUSCODE_INVALID, msg = '' and adr = NULL via memset. back_clear_entry (htsback.c:128) also sets INVALID.","htsrequest start (htslib.c:668-673) sets adr=NULL, size=0, msg='' and statuscode=STATUSCODE_NON_FATAL as the default.","Positive statuscode at htslib.c:759: for local file:// requests, statuscode = HTTP_OK and msg 'OK' as soon as the file opens, before any headers.","Main cause of a stale positive code: treatfirstline() (htslib.c:1238-1305) sets statuscode = HTTP_OK with msg 'Unknown, assuming junky server' in three cases: the status line is empty (the final else, htslib.c:~1300), the line starts with '<' (htslib.c:1280), and the line is whitespace-only (htslib.c:1289). The commented-out code at htslib.c:1296-1299 would have set STATUSCODE_INVALID with msg 'Empty reponse or internal error' instead.","Callers reach that branch when the socket closes early. htsrequest reads the status line with finput() at htslib.c:797-805; an EOF or empty read gives rcvd=='' and then treatfirstline(retour, rcvd) at htslib.c:807. http_test does the same at htslib.c:2090. Neither path checks for EOF first, so a closed connection gives statuscode=200, msg='Unknown, assuming junky server', and adr is still NULL (set at htslib.c:670).","In htsrequest, a send failure (htslib.c:1226-1230) only sets msg='Write error' and soc=INVALID_SOCKET. It does not change statuscode, which stays at NON_FATAL (-5) unless an earlier assignment changed it.","In the back_* path, the status line is parsed by treatfirstline at htsback.c:3599 and :3651, after http_xfread1(&r,0) has read the header block. Other places also set 200: htsback.c:3699 (203 becomes 200) and htsback.c:3744 (406 becomes 200).","Connection errors in back_wait set CONNERROR or NON_FATAL (htsback.c:2681-3027, 3315-3347) and timeouts set TIMEOUT (htsback.c:2579). I did not trace the retry logic itself.","http_xfread1 (htslib.c:~1860-1985) allocates r->adr as a header buffer (malloct(8192)) when it reads header bytes (htslib.c:1965, 1980) and sets INVALID at htslib.c:1866 and 1946. A closed connection with no data can therefore leave adr non-NULL, holding only that header buffer.","On r.adr == NULL for a successful empty 200 body: it is not guaranteed to be NULL. The header buffer from http_xfread1 is malloc'd and later reused or freed. htsback.c:3683 sets adr=NULL after header processing, and htsback.c:4208 mallocs 2 bytes in some case. A successful empty body may therefore have adr NULL or a tiny allocation, and size==0 is the reliable check."],"confidence":0.55}

content.text: Indentation differs in the second edit; I'll retry with the exact text.
Probably a whitespace mismatch; use a smaller anchor.

I changed `treatfirstline()` in `src/htslib.c` so an empty status line now gives `STATUSCODE_INVALID` instead of 200. I haven't built it or run any tests.

When a connection closes before the status line arrives, the status line is empty. `treatfirstline()` used to turn that into `HTTP_OK` with the message "Unknown, assuming junky server". That would also explain why `r.statuscode > 0` held on a connection that never answered. The save gate in `htscore.c` then ran `filesave()` on the empty body and truncated the file. With the failure status the gate skips the save, so the previous copy stays.

The edit sets the message to "Empty reponse or internal error", which is the text that was commented out in that branch. I didn't trace why this would show up only on macOS.

**Not changed:** a status line that is only whitespace still maps to 200. Four `edit_file` attempts on that branch failed with "old text not found", probably because of a whitespace or line-ending mismatch, so I left it. A connection that dies with no data at all gives an empty string, so it should take the fixed path.

**Risk:** `treatfirstline()` is shared by other request paths (`http_test` and the `back_*` code). They now see the failure status on an empty response instead of 200. I didn't check the retry logic for any other effect.
